subject.title: [Feature]: Pre-reset agentic memory flush — /new and daily reset should get the same memory flush as compaction

question: Should OpenClaw run a silent tool-capable memory-flush agent turn before explicit, daily, and idle resets, and what blocking/background/config/security boundaries should govern it?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the permanent behavior changes reset latency, silent model/tool execution, durable memory retention, plugin boundaries, and security expectations, so automation should not choose the policy alone.

options.title: Define a bounded pre-reset flush
options.body: Approve an explicit reset-memory policy with timeout, dedupe, opt-out/config, audit, sandbox, and security constraints before implementation.

options.title: Keep reset persistence mechanical
options.body: Treat session-memory hook improvements such as PR #61675 as the supported reset boundary and narrow or reject silent agent execution on reset.

options.title: Push continuity to memory plugins
options.body: Require memory plugins or MCP-backed memory services to own continuous persistence and extend only missing core lifecycle events or APIs.

recommendation.title: Define a bounded pre-reset flush
recommendation.body: Approve an explicit reset-memory policy with timeout, dedupe, opt-out/config, audit, sandbox, and security constraints before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to both the pre-compaction flush and daily reset policy history, making them the strongest owner for the cross-boundary product decision.
